Dear Hiring Team,

I'm applying for the Marketing Coordinator role at Maasmechelen Village.

I work where digital marketing, structure and content meet. Right now I handle SEO, CMS and content for client websites while running my own freelance projects end to end — which means tracking deadlines, keeping deliverables moving and being the person clients and colleagues come to with the practical questions. I'm digitally fluent across WordPress, CMS, analytics and reporting tools, and I use AI tools daily to speed up routine admin and catch problems early.

The connective part of this role — keeping projects and people aligned across channels — is the part I enjoy most. Being on site in Maasmechelen, close to where I live, makes it even more appealing.

One honest note: English is fluent, my Dutch is B1 in writing and improving.

I'd welcome the chance to talk.

cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Team,

Maasmechelen Village's Marketing Coordinator role reads like a description of how I already work: several projects and channels moving at once, being the person others rely on for the details, and using digital tools to make that easier rather than harder.

Over the past two years I've worked across SEO, content and web for clients — building and maintaining WordPress sites with Elementor and Rank Math, publishing pages, blog posts and product content, and reporting on results in Google Analytics and Search Console. Some of that work was coordination-heavy. For a pharmacists' association I built and maintained a consistent layout across roughly 600 member profile pages, and at Knowledge Experts I supported SharePoint-based digital workplace projects for ŞOK Market (4,000+ stores) and Aras Kargo (12,000 staff), where keeping structure and stakeholders aligned mattered as much as the build itself. I also designed and launched Shopify stores, handling catalogue, design and content together.

Structure is where I'm strongest. I like the unglamorous work of keeping a project tool honest, flagging a deadline that's about to slip, and making a clear call when priorities compete. I'm comfortable moving between CMS, social platforms, project boards and Office, and I use AI tools daily — for research, reporting and automating repetitive admin. My background as a front-end developer means I understand what the digital team needs technically, and I can pick up new tools, including video editing, quickly.

On languages: English is fluent, Turkish is native, and my Dutch is at B1 writing and A2+ speaking. I live in Zwijndrecht, close to the Village, and I'm actively improving my Dutch so I can use it more at work.

I'd like to bring that mix of structure, digital fluency and practical support to your team, and I'd welcome a conversation.

Warm regards,
Baver Ok

baverok@gmail.com
baverok.com | linkedin.com/in/baverok
cv_highlights:
- Two years across digital marketing, SEO and web, delivered for client websites at Episto and Knowledge Experts (KXP) — the 1–3 year experience the role asks for.
- CMS and channel operations: publishing and maintaining pages, blog posts and media in WordPress (Elementor, Astra, Rank Math), plus store design, catalogue and content for two Shopify stores.
- Coordination at scale: consistent layout for ~600 member profile pages at majistraleczacilari.org.tr; SharePoint digital workplace projects for ŞOK Market (4,000+ stores) and Aras Kargo (12,000 staff); front-end background (AngularJS, JavaScript) for technical understanding.
- AI and automation: daily LLM use for research, content and audits, prompt engineering, MCP integrations into WordPress and SEO tools, Python automation, and an Android app live on Google Play.
- Reporting and languages: Google Analytics, Search Console, Semrush, Ahrefs, Google Ads; English fluent, Turkish native, Dutch (writing B1, speaking A2+) and improving.
